messages:
Alex: Ran an arrival-variance sweep across the microbatch window parameters this morning. Noticed a weird knee where kernel selection flips and p99 jumps. Posting raw notes below.

Maria: link? short summary pls — is this KV-related or pure kernel/runtime?

Alex: TL;DR: with base microbatch-interval=3ms and coalesce-delay=8ms, adding jitter >~6ms causes kernel-picker to choose the slower generic path ~30% of the time. p50 up modestly, p99 spikes ~2-3x. KV hitrate also shows transient dips during high jitter runs.

TJ: hmm. Do you have the profiler traces? is the switch happening at batch-formation time or during dispatch?

Alex: dispatch. Short snippets:

```
# run config (sweep)
microbatch_interval=3ms
coalesce_delay=8ms
jitter = [0ms, 2ms, 6ms, 10ms]
queue_policy = FIFO
kernel_threshold.batch_size = 16
```

Observed metrics (approx):
- jitter=0ms: p50=28ms p95=82ms p99=190ms kernel_fused_ratio=0.92 kv_hit=0.995
- jitter=6ms: p50=34ms p95=120ms p99=360ms kernel_fused_ratio=0.63 kv_hit=0.97
- jitter=10ms: p50=48ms p95=210ms p99=480ms kernel_fused_ratio=0.41 kv_hit=0.93

Profile snippet (top stacks, diff between 0ms and 10ms):
- +120ms: kernel-selection / fallback overhead
- +80ms: memcpy / reorg when falling back to generic kernels
- +60ms: extra scheduling wait (microbatch alignment)
```

Sam: The KV dip makes sense: jitter scatters request arrival relative to our priming window so the prefix/kv cache isn't reused as often. We see intermittent kv misses that cause re-encoding / longer KV loads. Logs show TTL refills falling behind when jitter increases.

TJ: So two interacting effects: 1) arrival variance reduces effective coalesced batch sizes -> triggers different kernel branch, 2) misaligned arrivals reduce KV locality causing extra work. Both increase latency and change distribution.

Maria: Can we avoid the kernel flip by changing the kernel-picker heuristics? Maybe prefer fused kernel if expected batch size distribution is wide? Any safety/quality tradeoffs?

Alex: Quick experiment idea: add a hysteresis to kernel selection instead of instant flip. Pseudocode:

```
# kernel chooser (naive)
if est_batch_size >= B: choose fused
else: choose generic

# proposed: hysteresis + smoothing
smoothed_batch = EMA(batch_size, alpha=0.2)
if smoothed_batch >= B_low: prefer fused
if smoothed_batch < B_high: allow generic
# B_low < B_high to avoid flip-flop
```

Also try increasing kernel_threshold.batch_size by 2 to bias toward fused.

Sam: Also for KV: try bumping kv_keep_seconds from 30 -> 60 and add lightweight priming on cold-starts. That should reduce miss spikes during jitter bursts.

TJ: Another lever: queue policy. FIFO favors oldest-first which helps p99 when arrivals are bursty, but when arrival variance is high a size-based drain (drain when batch >= N) can stabilize kernel usage. Proposal:

```
if var(arrivals, last_window) > VAR_T:
  coalesce_delay = min(max_delay, base_delay * 1.5)
  drain_policy = size_or_time(N=12, T=coalesce_delay)
else:
  drain_policy = time_based(T=base_delay)
```

This makes the window adaptive rather than static.

Maria: Sounds reasonable. We should A/B the hysteresis change + kv_keep bump vs adaptive queue policy. Keep other knobs constant.

Alex: I'll spin up two jobs: (A) hysteresis + kv_keep=60, (B) adaptive-queue + kv_keep=60. Will log kernel_fused_ratio, kv_hit, p50/p95/p99, and flame diffs.

infra-bot: Test jobs created: run/1938200000-variance-hysteresis and run/1938200000-variance-adaptive (links: https://ci.internal/runs/1938200000-*) :white_check_mark:

Sam: small note — add KV priming script in warmup to both jobs. It's cheap and will show how much of the regression is purely KV vs kernel.

Alex: added priming. Expected run duration ~2h each. I'll post preliminary numbers here when done.

Maria: thanks — this matches what we feared but good to see concrete numbers. If hysteresis recovers p99 without sacrificing throughput, might be lowest-risk.

TJ: Action items:
- Alex: run the two experiments, attach profiler flame diffs (due EOD)
- Sam: prepare KV priming snippet + config bump for kv_keep_seconds
- Maria/TJ: design A/B analysis queries for kernel_fused_ratio vs latency buckets

Alex: noted. Will update thread with artifacts. :thumbsup:
